title: Prove rank factor 1 for every-stage paired-star gaps and raise the thin-rank bound to 2q⌈g/3⌉ (no κ)
body:
## Result

Scoped written proof with exact finite corroboration. No new κ, no word, no selected-frontier change.

unpaidmoon's open #7050 studies paired-star words with one internal thin gap in every stage. It proves that the own-leaf degree-1 core-to-leaf block has rank at most `2 rank(Z)`, deduces total thin rank at least `q g / 2`, and asks in its open question 1 whether the factor is 1 under the square condition `P_s Z P_f = 0` for every half width `q`. This package answers that question.

1. **Rank lemma.** For complementary idempotents `P + Q = I` over any field and any `Z` with `Q Z P = 0`: `rank(P Z P + Q Z Q) = rank(P Z P) + rank(Q Z Q) <= rank(Z)`. In a basis adapted to `im P ⊕ im Q`, `Z` is block triangular and the pinching is its block diagonal.
2. **Factor 1, sharp.** For every `q`, every `B12`, `B21` and either half order, the own-leaf degree-1 block has rank at most `rank(Z)`. With `B = 0` and `Z` the identity from the leaf into the core, the block is `I_{2q}` and `rank(Z) = 2q`, so 1 is the best constant at every `q`.
3. **Bound, conditional on #7050's schedule analysis.** A successful every-stage word has total thin rank at least `2 q ceil(g/3)`. At `g = 31`, `q = 26` this is **572**. #7050 proves 403, and its predicted factor-1 weight count would give `ceil(2 q g / 3) = 538`. The proof adds the per-leaf inequalities on leaves `0, 3, 6, ...`, whose contributing gaps are pairwise disjoint.

The same inequalities admit a covering point of value `2 q ceil(g/3)`, so rank counting on the core-to-leaf blocks gives nothing higher. That is a limit of the method. It is not a word, and 572 is not shown to be attained.

Package: `research/every-stage-gap-rank-factor` (`PROOF.md`, `README.md`, `verify.py`). Card `joint-query-controller`, priority revision 8, scope **changed**: the card asks for a changed query demand or caller, and this package answers a rank question on one fixed schedule family.

## Evidence and reproduction

From the repository root, CPython 3.12.15, standard library only:

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -W error -B research/every-stage-gap-rank-factor/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -O -W error -B research/every-stage-gap-rank-factor/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/every-stage-gap-rank-factor
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/every-stage-gap-rank-factor --check-source-history
```

Local results at head `26f8bbfb23feb1f24ba0eb3fb6c4187b331fa057`:

- both verifier modes end with `PASS_EVERY_STAGE_GAP_RANK_FACTOR factor=1 bound_g31_q26=572 certificate=e42b24ab6676fb20 no_new_kappa`, about 2.7 s each;
- `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE research/every-stage-gap-rank-factor outcome=completed`, 5.9 s for both registered commands;
- `PASS_RESEARCH_COMMIT_BYTES` with 6 files and source history commit `e54523517d0f03e58352e647c403a5af3e525a57`.

What the verifier checks, all exact:

- every 4 by 4 matrix over `F_2`, every `B`, both half orders: 524,288 cases, of which 32,768 satisfy the square condition; the lemma and the block bound hold on each;
- control: 168 of 1,800 rank-one cases have block rank 2, and each violates the square condition;
- 4,500 seeded random cases on the actual stage halves at `q = 2, 3, 4`;
- 3,200 seeded random cases of the lemma over `F_2`, `F_3`, `F_5`, `F_7`, each with a random submatrix;
- the sharpness witness at `q = 1, 2, 3, 5, 26`;
- 1,170 of 30,600 rank-one maps at `q = 1` satisfy the square condition and meet leaves `t-1`, `t`, `t+1` at rank one each;
- contributor sets recomputed from the monomials, disjointness and the covering point for every `g <= 64`, with two rejection controls.

The random cases corroborate the proof. They are not a census.

## Limitations and unrun obligations

- The bound in item 3 is conditional on #7050's schedule hypothesis, square condition and monomial comparison. Those are cited and were not audited or replayed. Only the exponent comparison for the contributor list is recomputed, from #7050's stated formulas.
- Nested and crossed stage intervals are outside the schedule.
- The leaf-to-core blocks are not used.
- No `g = 31`, `q = 26` word is constructed or excluded outside this schedule.
- No independent human review and no formal proof-kernel review. No Lean, Docker or selected-supplier replay was run.

## Open next questions

1. Do the leaf-to-core blocks raise the every-stage bound above `2 q ceil(g/3)`? First step: write the leaf-to-core degree-1 block of one internal gap under `P_s Z P_f = 0` and test whether a map that meets leaves `t-1`, `t`, `t+1` at full rank can also cancel its own leaf-to-core monomials.
2. Is total thin rank `2 q ceil(g/3)` compatible with the other monomials of the endpoint at `g = 3`, `q = 1`, where the bound is 2? First step: an exhaustive census of one internal map of rank at most 2 in stage 1 against every core-to-leaf monomial.
3. Does the block-triangular argument extend to nested or crossed intervals, where the square condition changes? First step: derive the squared-monomial condition for one nested pair.

## Related open work

- #7050 (unpaidmoon): source of the question, the schedule and the factor-2 bound 403. This package builds on it. On the shared `q = 1` domain the census here agrees with its two recorded observations: no excess under the square condition, and rank-one matrices with block rank 2 when the square is allowed.
- #7025 (unpaidmoon): one internal gap in at most one stage, bound `q(g-3) = 728`. A smaller schedule family; not replaced and not recomputed.
- #7005 (unpaidmoon): consecutive halves with no internal map, bound `q g = 806`. A smaller schedule family; not replaced and not recomputed.
- #7053 (unpaidmoon): one rank-`q` internal map and the external bound `q(g-1)`. A different schedule; no shared number.
- #7085 and #7084 (unpaidmoon): one interleaved `g = 31`, `q = 26` word, and nested and crossed pure products. Outside the every-stage hypothesis; no shared number.
- #7010 (unpaidmoon): adjacent halves need `ceil(g/2)` thin maps. A map-count bound on a different schedule; no shared number.

## Credit

unpaidmoon's #7050 supplies the schedule, the square condition, the degree-1 block, the monomial comparison, the factor-2 bound, the `q = 1` census observation and the question. unpaidmoon's #7025 and #7005 supply the neighbouring bounds. The paired-star contract and the commuting map-count are from Ali Romman's #5747 with its predecessors #5673, #5631 and #5617, and Cinna Davis supplied the controller and simplex lineage those packages retain. The rank inequality for block triangular matrices is classical. This contribution was produced by Nick Petalas.

## CI notes

CI did not certify this package. At head `26f8bbfb23feb1f24ba0eb3fb6c4187b331fa057`, [run 42905330981](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/42905330981) failed in the `plan` job ([job 130141720290](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/42905330981/job/130141720290)), and the package `replay` job was skipped because `plan` failed.

The failing step is "Onboarding helper tests": 760 tests ran, 1 failed, 24 were skipped. The one failure is

```text
FAIL: test_current_ci_section_matches_selected_record (test_research_current_status.CurrentCiNavigationTests.test_current_ci_section_matches_selected_record)
AssertionError: '`make frontier7000-verify`' not found in '# CI verification\n\n## Current selected-family replay: #6030 ...'
```

The cause is on main, in files this PR does not touch. At base `e54523517d0f03e58352e647c403a5af3e525a57`, `certificates/selected-result.json` has `"reproduce": "make frontier7000-verify"`, while `docs/ci-verification.md` still opens with "Current selected-family replay: #6030". This PR changes only `research/every-stage-gap-rank-factor/`.

The same single test is the only failure, with the same 760-test count, in three other runs read from their logs: [42905094314](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/42905094314) (#7124), [42903313790](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/42903313790) (#7123) and [42905202459](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/42905202459) (#7125).

No fix or retrigger was pushed. The evidence for this package is the local run recorded above: both registered commands pass in under 3 s each.
